sentences.show: An army set out to free Jerusalem. Instead, it attacked a Christian city, to pay off a bill.
The siege of Zara began on this day in 1202.
The Fourth Crusade had ordered a fleet from Venice for 35,000 men.
Only about 12,000 showed up. They couldn't pay.
Venice's old, blind doge, Enrico Dandolo, offered a deal: capture Zara for us.
Zara was a Catholic city, under the Pope's own protection.
The Pope wrote, forbidding it, and threatened excommunication. Most crusaders went anyway.
The people of Zara hung crosses on their walls, to show they were Christians too.
It made no difference. Two weeks later, the city fell, and was sacked.
The Pope excommunicated the entire army.
And the crusade never reached Jerusalem. Its next target was Constantinople.
Also on this day: Stanley found Doctor Livingstone, and the Edmund Fitzgerald sank in Lake Superior.
